restrictions: Messages are exactly 64 bytes (one root block, flags 11, length 64, counter 0).
Grouped birthday: 2^96 groups; shared m0..m14; enumerate all m15.

Retained prefixes[g] table stores packed m0..m14 (two 256-bit words) per group; written at group setup; read on VERIFY. Live BT record recs[s]=(g||m15) reconstructs the 64-byte message via prefixes[g] — repairs 7212 EVAL-F1/F-MSG-RECONSTRUCTION.

K_full is the full 256-bit partial-eval digest. Briggs-Torczon sparse set indexes by top 140 bits; sparse entries are 256-bit words; never clears sparse[]; membership via dense[sparse[idx]]==idx and sparse[idx]<n.
Unequal-K index hits discard with Word ops only (no target compression). Equal K_full triggers VERIFY (§2.5): rebuild both messages via prefix table, then two reference compressions; V_max=8.

Per-message Word ops = 293 = 252 inner + 14 pack + 24 BT/K-compare + 3 loop. Group setup <=512 Word/group => <2^97 units. VERIFY Word work <=640 => <2 units. T_ver compressions <=16. No expectations in T.
Declared score-critical heuristics: H1-grouped-digests (probability only) and H-COST-BT-SPARSE (24-op BT envelope, same Briggs-Torczon procedure as 03e49 with tightened address margin).
F2 is earliest-completing colliding-pair displacement (Pr<=2^-12 under H1), with pair selection defined in proof §4.
Undercut of 03e49dc5 family (297→293 ops) by honest BT address-margin trim 28→24. Does NOT revive c367 H-COST-SPARSE-21. Retains c145/4dd/c367-BT/7212 repairs. Unkeyed BLAKE3-256; 2 rounds.

heuristics.statement: For uniformly random independent group prefixes and exhaustive m15 enumeration, the 2^128 digests behave like independent uniform 256-bit strings for bounding F1, the earliest-completing-pair F2 displacement probability conditional on existence of a collision, and F4, up to a negligible additive gap covered by the allowance between the model bound (>0.3932) and claimed success probability 0.39.
heuristics.scope: Success-probability claim only. Does not justify expectation-for-worst-case substitutions in the time bound. Includes the F2 conditioning claim that earliest-completing-pair selection does not inflate the N/2^140 occupancy bound under this independent-uniform model.
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer matched-scale digest-xor-mask experiments at widths 16, 20, and 24 with N_t^2/2^w=1, plus single-group stress, are consistency checks only. They do not rigorously establish full-scale 256-bit iid behavior over 2^128 structured messages; that step remains the modeling content of this heuristic.
heuristics.limitations: H1 unproved. Truncation cannot detect almost-permutations. No full-scale collision known. Experiments expressly do not support iid success-probability or full-scale inference (CRYPT-H1 / EXP-EXT gaps acknowledged).

heuristics.statement: On the classical 256-bit word RAM of collision-frontier-v5, the Briggs-Torczon procedure in proof §2.4 implements membership test (dense[sparse[idx]]==idx and sparse[idx]<n), insert of (idx,K_full,g||m15), and unequal-K discard for a top-140-bit index with never-cleared sparse[] of 256-bit words in at most 24 charged primitive word operations per message, including one 256-bit K_full compare and address-arithmetic margin. Message reconstruction is out of scope for this heuristic (it uses the prefixes table in VERIFY, charged separately).
heuristics.scope: Only the 24-op BT envelope inside the 293-ops/msg candidate ledger. Does not cover partial-eval inner body, group-setup prefix writes, VERIFY reconstruction Word ops, or reference compressions. Same procedure family as the 28-op envelope accepted as established/plausible on 03e49dc5; the haircut is address-margin only (10→6), not a return to undeclared H-COST-SPARSE-21.
heuristics.extrapolation: Standard Briggs-Torczon correctness (dense[sparse[i]]==i filter) extrapolated to word-addressable sparse[0..2^140) without an initialization pass. Analytic from the §2.4 op list and path table; no empirical RAM microbenchmark.
heuristics.limitations: Not empirically microbenchmarked. If word-addressing a 2^140 sparse table required multi-op page walks beyond the 24-op margin, the ledger would need a higher BT charge (fallback: restore 28-op / 297 / 127.467).
